clue.text: New resolutions broken by good doctors

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the letters that follow are put into a fresh order
a thing broken is smashed apart, and here the letter added from the next word is mixed into the pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Physicians have given up on their New Year's resolutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good doctors' reads as one phrase, but good only supplies a letter and doctors alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurologists are medical specialists in the nervous system, so they are a kind of doctor.

clue.text: More stylish pattern if tie revamps clothes

indicators.note: as a verb, clothes means wraps around, so the answer sits dressed inside the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of pattern, all of if and tie, and the start of revamps

explanation.surface: A patterned tie could give your outfit a smarter look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun about fashion, but it is a verb saying the words wrap the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty is informal for smart or stylish, and the comparative form matches 'more stylish'.

clue.text: Metallic element, you heard, put on skull, but not roughly

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound, so the pronoun is replaced by the single letter that sounds the same
roughly stands for the abbreviation of circa, and 'but not' tells us to leave that letter out

blocks.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you
the cranium is the skull
c. for circa, Latin for roughly or about

explanation.surface: Odd instructions about placing a heavy metal on a skull, not too roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put on' means placed above, so the sound-alike letter sits above the shortened skull word.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium is a heavy radioactive chemical element classed among the metals.

clue.text: Protest that is about Vardy's header creating goal

indicators.note: a header is the top of a word in a down clue, so only its opening letter is kept
about means surrounding, so the abbreviation wraps round the letter taken next

blocks.note: to object is to protest
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
the first letter of the footballer's name

explanation.surface: A football complaint about whether striker Jamie Vardy's headed goal should stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Jamie Vardy is an English footballer, and 'header' and 'goal' both play on the football picture while doing other jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective is an aim or target, the same as a goal one is working towards.

clue.text: Formerly working with Anglican group

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Someone who used to work alongside a church group.
explanation.definitionFit: Once as an adverb means at some time in the past, the same as formerly.

clue.text: Unstable cover put around middle of deck

indicators.note: the middle of a word means just its central letters are used
putting something around another encloses it, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: to insure is to give cover against loss
the two central letters of deck

explanation.surface: A wobbly tarpaulin has been put round the middle of a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like a tarpaulin in the surface, but it means insurance cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means not firmly fixed or likely to give way, which is unstable.

clue.text: Rigged vote securing Republican a store of wealth

indicators.note: a rigged result has been fixed and tampered with, so the letters are rearranged
to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so these letters take in the abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A fixed election lets a Republican keep a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a valuable collection, as in treasure trove, so it is a store of riches.

clue.text: Former PM cutting former monarch's shaggy hair

indicators.note: cutting something removes part of it, so the royal abbreviation is trimmed away

blocks.note: Margaret Thatcher, British Prime Minister 1979 to 1990
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A previous Prime Minister trimming the unkempt locks of a past king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the final ER from THATCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is an informal word for a thick, untidy head of hair, likened to roof straw.

clue.text: Tyrannous ruler from French location

blocks.note: de is French for from
a spot is a place or location

explanation.surface: A tyrant who comes from a place in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like a link word, but it is the word to translate into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, a tyrant.

clue.text: Knave in agitated state with small cakes

blocks.note: to be in a flap is to be in a panic
the jack is the knave in a pack of cards
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A rogue in a panic over some little cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knave in agitated state' is read as a knave in a flap, so the panic word is written first.
explanation.definitionFit: Flapjacks are oat-and-syrup bar cakes in Britain, or pancakes in America.

clue.text: It's primarily orange coloured, having reddish earth?

definitions.text: It's primarily orange coloured, having reddish earth?

indicators.note: primarily suggests first of all, so only the opening letter of each following word counts

blocks.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Something mostly orange in colour, made from reddish soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the description of the pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment of iron oxide, ranging from yellow to orange-brown or red.

clue.text: Current do-it-yourself stores firm about silliness

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the company abbreviation faces the other way
a thing that stores something keeps it inside, so the home-improvement letters hold the next piece

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
DIY is the common abbreviation
Co. abbreviates company, a firm

explanation.surface: Present-day home-improvement shops are full of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day, but it is the physics symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocy is foolish behaviour, which is silliness.

clue.text: Some of pirates' crew to posture, showing a bit of bottle

indicators.note: some of means only part of the words that follow is used, so the answer lies inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of pirates' through crew and to into the start of posture

explanation.surface: Swaggering pirates show a little courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of bottle' looks like British slang for some courage, but it means part of a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw top is the threaded cap or lid of a bottle, a part of it.

clue.text: Stay at home after dealing with case of malaria

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters of the next word are used

blocks.note: re means concerning or dealing with
the first and last letters of malaria
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Stay indoors after treating a malaria case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' sounds like part of the instruction to stay, but it supplies the final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay where one is.

clue.text: Note needlework absorbs time

indicators.note: absorbing something takes it inside, so the needlework word holds the letter

blocks.note: crochet is needlework made with a hooked needle
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A reminder that sewing takes up a lot of one's time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' reads as observe, but it is a musical note; T goes after CRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note of one beat, a quarter note in American usage.

clue.text: Wonderful introduction to technical work by artist

indicators.note: an introduction is the beginning, so only the first letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of technical
op. abbreviates opus, a work
a drawer is someone who draws

explanation.surface: Praise for an artist's piece introducing a technical skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' here means one who draws, not the sliding box in a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an informal British term for the very best or highest quality, so first-rate.

clue.text: Flammable liquid soldier with nasty smell brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top, so the smell word runs backwards

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
niff is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A soldier smelling of fuel has been sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' suggests vomiting, but it is the upward-reading signal; niff is British slang for a pong.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is the British name for kerosene, a flammable oil used as fuel.

clue.text: Hindering American plugging remix of Whitney

indicators.note: plugging a hole fills it, so this letter goes inside the rearranged name
a remix reworks a recording, so the singer's name is put in a new order

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American is getting in the way by promoting a Whitney Houston remix.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes into the rearranged WHITNEY just before the final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the way is an obstruction, which is what hindering describes.

clue.text: Forged coin given to the setter for pay

indicators.note: a forged coin is a fake, made up afresh, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: Someone hands the crossword compiler a counterfeit coin as wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is money received for work, which is pay.

clue.text: Child filled with energy upset father's brewing vessel

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down clue turned upside down, so the word for father reads in reverse
a thing filled with something holds it inside, so the child word holds the other letters

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
E is the symbol for energy
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A hyperactive child knocked over Dad's tea things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' paints a spill, but it turns the father word over; the inserted letters go after the child word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapot is the pot in which tea is brewed.

clue.text: Irritability created by poor sleep before noon

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are put into a different form

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Bad temper caused by a bad night's sleep before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' puts the noon letter after the rearranged sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen means bad temper or peevishness, the organ once thought to be the seat of anger.

clue.text: Notable contemporary artist with eastern scripture

blocks.note: Tracey Emin, the British contemporary artist
E is the abbreviation for eastern
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A distinguished modern painter who works with Eastern sacred texts.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a famous British artist and a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means famous and respected in a field, which is notable.

clue.text: Irritated Liberal required drinks

indicators.note: drinking something takes it in, so the word for required swallows the letter

blocks.note: needed means required
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal was irked by needing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinks' looks like a noun but is the verb telling us one piece takes in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to annoy them persistently, so needled means irritated.

clue.text: President's extremely childish flier

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of childish
an airman is a pilot or flyer

explanation.surface: A president's pilot behaves very immaturely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' reads as very, but it keeps only the ends of childish.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman presides over a meeting or company, and a president holds the same role.

clue.text: Archly, Amber regularly ignored what Larry and Barry do

indicators.note: ignoring letters at regular intervals means every other letter is dropped and the rest are kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A knowing Amber is overlooked by two men named Larry and Barry.
explanation.walkthrough: Larry and Barry look like people in the story, but the definition is about their names sounding alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Larry and Barry share the same ending sound, so as words they rhyme with each other.

clue.text: Loudly begs for adulatory comments

indicators.note: loudly means spoken out, so we want a word that sounds like the next one when said

blocks.note: to pray is to beg or plead

explanation.surface: Someone noisily pleads for flattering remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is approving or admiring words, which adulatory comments are.

clue.text: What turned up on record, a Beatles album

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means flipped to read upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: eh? is an exclamation meaning what?
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Asking which Beatles album showed up on vinyl.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the reversed EH above the record letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Help! is the Beatles' 1965 album, which accompanied their film of the same name.

clue.text: Temperamental and low, deny losing heart

indicators.note: losing its heart means the word gives up its central letters

blocks.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone moody and depressed refuses to lose courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' seems to mean sad, but it is the cow's call. DENY drops its middle EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Moody describes someone whose temper changes unpredictably, which is temperamental.

clue.text: After complimentary whiskey, scoundrel is to take it easy

blocks.note: complimentary means free of charge
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a heel is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A rogue relaxes after a free glass of whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places HEEL after the first two pieces. Whiskey stands for W because it is the NATO radio code word for that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To freewheel is to coast without pedalling, so figuratively to act with little effort.

clue.text: Malicious president with aim to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spiteful president sets out to overhaul things.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean-spirited describes someone ungenerous and spiteful, which is close to malicious.
